subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Integral Control: Eliminating Steady-State Error
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Integral Control: Eliminating Steady-State Error.

hook.text: Proportional control gets close but not exact. Integral control accumulates the remaining error and fixes it.

buildup.text: The integral term sums all past errors over time. Even a tiny persistent error grows until corrected.

discovery.text: This drives steady-state error to zero — the integral action doesn't stop until the error is gone.

twist.text: Integral windup occurs if the actuator saturates — the integral keeps growing, causing massive overshoot later.

climax.text: Anti-windup techniques clamp the integral term when the actuator is maxed out.

punchline.text: Sum the error over time — integral control never settles for close enough.

quiz.question: What is integral windup?
options: The integral term oscillates at high frequency
The integral accumulates excessively during actuator saturation, causing later overshoot
The integral term decreases over time due to friction
